title: Reliability intake: degradation tolerance & fallback alignment — Auriga Technologies
summary: Initial reliability-focused discovery for evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Customer emphasized strict 99.9% availability for latency-sensitive endpoints, preference for private deployment for data residency, and interest in automated fallback policies and multi-region steering. Agreed to pilot plus a technical deep-dive and receive SOC2 docs and pricing appendix.
topics: SLO targets and p99/p999 latency expectations
Fallback matrix: model variant fallbacks, regional failover, and degraded-mode responses
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (security, latency, cost)
Traffic steering, sticky sessions, and cache priming
Monitoring, audit logs, and SOC2/ISO requirements
Pilot scope, benchmark plan, and success criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, uh diego from our se team will do the deep stuff later. how's everyone's afternoon?
[00:07] Karen (Auriga - CTO): good thanks, we have about 50 minutes — lots to cover around availability and what happens when things go south.
[00:12] Diego (Redwood SE): morning/afternoon all, quick agenda: align SLOs, review fallback topologies, and then fit for private deployment. we'll also call out what we recommend for a pilot.
[00:20] Karen: perfect. quick context: auriga's product is latency sensitive, gen-summary endpoints, 20ms median, 120ms p95 is our target in normal ops. but we care most about user-facing timeouts and graceful degradation.
[00:30] Naveen (Auriga - SRE): and to be explicit we need 99.9% availability on the inference path for a gold tier, otherwise internal SLAs kick in.
[00:37] Lina (Auriga - PM): also we have data residency in eu, so private or vpc-hosted options matter.
[00:43] Maya: ok good, that helps. quick question — is the traffic single-region today? or multi-region?
[00:48] Karen: mostly single region (eu-west) with failover to us-west for DR. but failovers are manual today and that's causing long blips.
[00:57] Diego: got it — manual failover is common. redwood supports automated multi-region steering and can do model variant fallbacks. quick layman example: if your preferred high-accuracy model is saturated, we can fall back to a quantized variant or a lower-latency model with a quality tag.
[01:10] Karen: how do you keep degrade behavior predictable? we don't want sudden quality cliffs.
[01:14] Diego: yeah that's the tricky part — we use a fallback matrix: route by policy (latency threshold, error rate, or capacity), prefer model variants validated by your eval set; we can do percentage-based traffic splitting during rollout so you can observe quality delta. also you can pin routes for specific customers.
[01:29] Naveen: and if region is down entirely, do you have an async queue/backpressure mechanism? we can't just drop requests.
[01:36] Diego: we have a few options: 1) redirect to another region with region-steering (best-effort, preserves sync latency but cross-region cost), 2) degrade to cached/fallback responses — prefix caching or KV cache for repeated prompts, 3) queue with SLA-based retry where we try for N seconds before returning degrade payload. preference depends on SLO and user experience.
[01:55] Karen: hmm our product needs <300ms tail for interactive flows; anything that adds cross-region RTT is concerning.
[02:01] Maya: that's where Dedicated or Private can help — you get capacity headroom and colocated hosts to avoid cross-region hops. Hosted can still do it but with network cost and more variability.
[02:11] Lina: cost question — if we do automatic fallback across regions, is that expensive?
[02:15] Maya: it can be, yes. cross-region inference increases egress and sometimes model runtime differences. Redwood Optimize suggests quantized fallbacks for cost-sensitive lanes and can auto-tune batching windows.
[02:25] Naveen: on security: we need KMS/HSM, audit logs, and SSO with SCIM; is that available for hosted?
[02:31] Diego: hosted offers SOC2 and standard audit logs; VPC/private gives you customer-managed KMS/HSM and stricter network controls. SSO/SCIM and RBAC are supported at both tiers, but private supports on-prem HSM.
[02:43] Karen: show of hands — are people comfortable with a plan that includes brief partial degradation, e.g., return a shorter summary or cached answer, rather than cross-region hop?
[02:50] Lina: i think yes as long as we can measure and label it in telemetry — we need to see how often degrade happens.
[02:57] Diego: absolutely, we expose token-level cost and latency breakdowns and tag degraded responses so you can alert.
[03:03] Maya: can i ask about traffic profile — naveen, what's your QPS and concurrency pattern?
[03:08] Naveen: peak is around 120 rps for the gen endpoint, fairly spiky. 99th percentile usage happens in bursts tied to business hours.
[03:16] Diego: with 120 rps you probably want dedicated pools for predictable p99, unless you architect heavy prefix caching. we can simulate with our benchmark harness and show p99 differences by deployment mode.
[03:27] Karen: okay, let's talk pilot. we want a low-friction pilot that tests fallback rules, region steering, and private fit.
[03:35] Maya: recommended pilot: 2 weeks, run in eu-west primarily, two fallback policies (model-variant fallback and regional failover), and a synthetic traffic run for chaos scenarios. measure p50/p95/p99 and degraded-rate.
[03:46] Lina: do you offer chaos tools or do we provide traffic simulation?
[03:49] Diego: we can provide a harness and scripts; you'll provide representative prompt sets and traffic patterns. we can also run a controlled partial outage to validate auto-fallbacks.
[03:59] Karen: what about rollbacks and canarying? we need to control automatic rollbacks if quality dips beyond threshold.
[04:05] Diego: built-in — you can set quality regression thresholds tied to your eval prompts. if fallback causes more than X% degradation on golden prompts, it auto-rolls back.
[04:15] Naveen: latency SLOs — we need to map contractual 99.9% to internal SRE alerts. can you give example SLO mapping?
[04:21] Maya: yes, we'll provide a sample SLO mapping doc: map 99.9% availability to 43 minutes monthly downtime, breaks down by region, define severity pages for p99 breach, and lay out on-call runbooks.
[04:33] Karen: ok great. can you also show us a sample fallback matrix? like if model A p99>350ms then model B; if region down then model C in us-west; if both then cached short answer.
[04:44] Diego: yes, i'll share a canonical matrix with rules and thresholds — we can parametrize thresholds.
[04:49] Lina: one more: data residency — if we failover to us-west, are we breaching residency?
[04:54] Maya: valid concern — we can configure steering to avoid cross-region failover for eu customers; in that case we prefer degrade/no cross-region. alternatively, private deployment with geo-replication is an option.
[05:05] Karen: that's what i expected. we may accept occasional longer tail in exchange for residency guarantees.
[05:10] Naveen: encryption in transit and at rest — is KMS used for prefixes/cache?
[05:15] Diego: yes, caches are encrypted; private gives you customer-managed KMS. hosted uses redwood-managed keys unless otherwise arranged with an enterprise contract.
[05:24] Maya: quick note on observability — we surface request traces, token timelines, model identity, and fallback tag. you'll get an alerting integration and we can push to your datadog/splunk.
[05:33] Karen: nice. how do we validate quality delta between models? we have a golden prompt set.
[05:37] Diego: we'll run A/B on the golden set and give you quantitative metrics (ROUGE/BLEU or your custom eval) plus human spot checks.
[05:44] Lina: do you support tying rollback thresholds to those eval metrics?
[05:47] Diego: yes, you can set eval-based thresholds as part of rollouts.
[05:51] Maya: timebox — we've gone 6 minutes. any critical open questions?
[05:55] Karen: cost math — send dedicated vs hosted delta with examples for 120 rps and for bursty traffic.
[05:59] Maya: will do.
[06:01] Naveen: action items on our side: share prompt corpus, and p99 target table.
[06:06] Maya: noted. i'll send SOC2 + ISO and the pilot proposal.
[06:10] Lina: can we get that by monday?
[06:12] Maya: yes, monday EOD — i'll include pricing appendix.
[06:15] Karen: ok next steps sound good. thanks everyone.
[06:18] Maya: cool i'll follow up shortly with docs and schedule the technical deep dive for next week.
[06:22] Diego: thanks, bye.
